Ready coverage is preserved: the local pre-push still derives the governing Issue acceptance criteria from GitHub and fails closed (DRAFT-ONLY) unless every Issue #442 criterion is covered. The hotfix makes that derivation match hosted admission exactly: criteria are read from the canonical base repository (upstream preferred over the fork), bound to the pushed remote branch ref rather than the local checkout, malformed/unreadable evidence fails closed to DRAFT-ONLY instead of crashing the boundary, and a push binding more than one distinct Issue is readiness-ambiguous (DRAFT-ONLY) rather than selecting a matching claim.
No hosted prerequisite/controller logic changes; exact-head hosted CI remains the proof for this head.
No new defect-registry family is added; the preflight guard still validates the registry.
No validation proof reuse surface is changed during this PR; the pre-push boundary keeps using hosted exact-head preflight as proof.
The DFF-019 family and its 21 railway-runtime bootstrap regressions are untouched; the hotfix does not enter the Railway runtime bootstrap code.

findings.evidence: The local pre-push derived the criteria repository by preferring 'origin', which in a fork workflow is the contributor fork; hosted Candidate Admission reads the governing Issue from the canonical base repository the PR targets. Fixed by preferring the upstream remote (with origin retained as the direct-clone fallback) so the governing Issue's acceptance criteria are fetched from the canonical repository only; regression tests assert origin=fork, upstream=canonical.

The local pre-push bound the governing Issue to the checked-out local branch name instead of the pushed remote branch ref the pull request head actually binds; with a differing local checkout the report could measure readiness against the wrong Issue. Fixed by binding coverage to the pushed refs/heads refs from the pre-push update lines, matching hosted admission; mismatched claim-vs-pushed binding fails closed to DRAFT-ONLY.

Malformed or unreadable review evidence (top-level array, non-object claims, corrupt JSON) previously raised AttributeError/GitEvidenceUnavailable inside the reporting path and could abort an ordinary Draft push. Fixed by explicit structural validation routing such evidence to DRAFT-ONLY; regressions assert no crash, ordinary Draft push continues, and READY-ELIGIBLE is never produced.

A single pre-push invocation could push the same HEAD to multiple remote branches bound to different Issues (e.g. issue-442-* and issue-444-*) and still report READY-ELIGIBLE when the review claim matched one of them, although hosted Candidate Admission evaluates each pushed head independently and would reject the other. Fixed: a push binding more than one distinct Issue now fails closed to DRAFT-ONLY before any claim is consulted; the verdict and reason are ordering-independent, and single-Issue multi-ref pushes are unchanged.
